scheme_name: Credit Card Scheme For Artisans And Weavers Of Handicrafts And Handloom Sector
description:
The Credit Card Scheme for Artisans and Weavers of Handicrafts and Handloom Sector was launched by the Government of India in 2003.

This scheme aims to provide financial assistance to artisans and weavers engaged in the handicrafts and handloom sectors.

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the income and livelihood of artisans and weavers.

The scheme facilitates access to credit for artisans and weavers who often face challenges in obtaining loans from traditional banking channels.

Under this scheme, artisans and weavers can avail of a credit limit of up to INR 1 lakh.

The scheme is designed to support both individual artisans and weaver groups.

The scheme also encourages the promotion of traditional crafts and textiles.

The government aims to empower artisans and weavers by providing them with the necessary financial resources.

The assistance provided under this scheme can be used for purchasing raw materials, tools, and equipment.

The scheme also aims to improve the overall productivity and quality of handicrafts and handloom products.

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on artisans and weavers who are engaged in traditional crafts.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old to qualify for the scheme.

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants.

Artisans and weavers must possess a valid identity proof and address proof.

Income criteria for eligibility are set at an annual income of up to INR 1 lakh.

The scheme is open to both individual artisans and registered cooperative societies of artisans and weavers.

The application process involves several steps.

Interested applicants must first obtain an application form from the nearest bank branch or the official website.

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents.

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, income proof, and a certificate of craft or weaving.

Once the application is submitted, the bank will assess the eligibility of the applicant.

The bank may conduct a field verification to evaluate the applicant's craft or weaving activities.

Upon successful verification, the bank will sanction the credit limit.

The disbursement of funds is typically done in a single installment.

The funds can be utilized for various purposes related to the handicraft and handloom business.

The repayment period for the loan is generally set at 3 years.

Interest rates on the loans under this scheme are competitive and vary from bank to bank.

The government provides a subsidy on the interest rates for eligible beneficiaries.

The subsidy can be as high as 7 percent for certain categories of artisans and weavers.

This makes the effective interest rate significantly lower for beneficiaries.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India.

The National Handloom Development Corporation is one of the key implementing agencies.

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme.

They assist in the identification of beneficiaries and facilitate the application process.

The scheme has been instrumental in providing financial support to over 1 lakh artisans and weavers since its inception.

As of 2023, the scheme has seen a steady increase in the number of beneficiaries each year.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 200 crores for the current financial year to support this scheme.

This allocation is aimed at expanding the reach of the scheme to more artisans and weavers.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of skill development and training.

Workshops and training sessions are organized to enhance the skills of artisans and weavers.

These training programs focus on improving the quality of products and introducing new techniques.

The scheme has been praised for its role in preserving traditional crafts and promoting cultural heritage.

The government regularly monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and efficiency.

Beneficiaries are encouraged to provide feedback on the scheme for continuous improvement.

The scheme has also been linked with various digital initiatives.

This includes the use of technology for better access to credit and market linkages.

Artisans and weavers are encouraged to use digital platforms for marketing their products.

The scheme has contributed to the overall growth of the handicrafts and handloom sector in India.

The handicrafts sector contributes approximately INR 23,000 crores to the Indian economy annually.

The handloom sector employs over 43 lakh people across the country.

The Credit Card Scheme for Artisans and Weavers is a significant step towards financial inclusion.

It empowers artisans and weavers to become self-reliant and improve their living standards.

The government continues to explore ways to enhance the benefits of this scheme.

This includes increasing the credit limit and expanding the eligibility criteria.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote the Make in India campaign.

This campaign aims to boost domestic manufacturing and create jobs.

The Credit Card Scheme for Artisans and Weavers is a vital component of this initiative.

Overall, the scheme has made a positive impact on the lives of many artisans and weavers across India.
